correctedState:
The finding's state is accurate; three refinements, all of which widen it rather than narrow it.

1. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` produces submission `{message:"/skill-b do XYZ", customSlashCommandId:"custom:skill:skill-a"}` (custom-slash-command-submission.ts:20-34), which the RPC expands via skillSlashCommandBody into the model message `[skill:skill-a] /skill-b do XYZ` (rpc/sessions.ts:335, custom-commands.ts:302-304). parseSkillMentionReferences on that string returns exactly ["skill-a"]; on `[skill:skill-a] [skill:skill-b] do XYZ` it returns ["skill-a","skill-b"]. So one skill loads and `/skill-b` is literal argument text. Claude's own skills.md:467 names this the pre-v2.1.199 behaviour.

2. THE NEAREST NATIVE EQUIVALENT ALSO DIVERGES, ON A SECOND AXIS. Nessy does support several skills in one turn through `[skill:...]` mentions (the @-mention composer path and the model-emitted path), but the arguments are PARTITIONED between mentions, not handed whole to each. runtimeSkillArguments (capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:606-616) is documented as "Arguments following the last matching `[skill:...]` reference, up to the next skill mention", and measured on `[skill:skill-a] [skill:skill-b] do XYZ` it yields "" for skill-a and "do XYZ" for skill-b. Claude's contract is "passes the trailing text to each as arguments" - the same text to every stacked skill. So closing this gap is two changes, not one: parse a run of leading skill commands, AND give each the same trailing text.

3. NO CAP EXISTS TO ADJUST. Claude bounds the run at six (first plus five, skills.md:469) and stops expansion at the first token that is not an inline user-invocable skill - explicitly ending at a forked-subagent skill such as /code-review (v2.1.218) or one whose arguments may themselves begin with a slash, such as /loop. Nessy has no such run, hence no cap and no stop rule; both would be new.

Scope note: the Electron composer is the only invocation surface - apps/cli has no slash-command path - so the fix has exactly one entry point, but the singular `customSlashCommandId` is baked into the SEND_MESSAGE RPC signature (rpc/sessions.ts:310), the SessionManager interface (session-manager-interface.ts:144) and four renderer prop types, so the wire changes with it.
